data:
Learn how the SlapRF software and hardware fit together, then install the SlapRF Timing Application on your phone or computer.
Architecture & Modes Understand Software vs. Hardware, Bluetooth Mode vs. USB Mode, and multi-gate splits. Installation Install SlapRF on Android, Windows, macOS, Linux, or Raspberry Pi.
SlapRF separates race logic on your phone or laptop from raw 5.8 GHz signal measurement at the gates, giving you low-cost hardware on the course and full race analytics at the pilot bench.
data.bluetooth-vs-usb-mode#Bluetooth vs. USB:
A SlapRF track uses one Hub timer (H1) and up to 6 optional Spoke timers (T1 through T6). Both Hub modes support single-gate lap timing and multi-gate section split timing.
Bluetooth ModeUSB Mode Bluetooth Mode (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin) removes all cables between the track and the pilot bench.
Power the Bluetooth Hub (H1) from a LiPo battery (via a 5 V USB-C BEC) or USB power bank and place it directly at the Start / Finish gate. Your phone or laptop stays with you at the bench and connects over Bluetooth Low Energy. Optional Spoke timers (T1 to T5) at split gates link to the Hub over 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW, and the Hub forwards every gate reading over Bluetooth.
USB Mode (slaprf-xiao-c5.bin) connects the Hub directly to your laptop or Android phone over a USB-C data cable for minimum transport latency.
The host USB port powers H1 directly with no battery required at the bench. Battery-powered Spoke timers (T1 to T6) sit at the track gates, including Start / Finish. If your USB cable reaches the Start / Finish gate, you can also place H1 directly on the Start / Finish gate in the Track editor.
data.mode-comparison#Mode Comparison: Aspect Bluetooth Hub USB Hub Firmware Image slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin slaprf-xiao-c5.bin Host Connection Wireless Bluetooth LE USB-C data cable Hub Power Source LiPo + 5 V BEC (or power bank) Host phone or laptop USB port Typical Placement At the Start / Finish gate At the pilot bench (or Start / Finish via cable) Wireless Spokes Up to 5 Spokes + Hub (6 gates) Up to 6 Spokes Transport Latency Low (ideal for solo & club practice) Lowest (ideal for formal race heats) Tip For everyday practice, Bluetooth Mode is the fastest field setup: place one battery-powered Hub at the Start / Finish gate, connect from your phone at the bench, and fly. For formal race heats where lowest wired latency matters most, use a USB Hub.
data.system-overview#System Overview:
Gate timers (H1 and T1 through T6) sweep up to 8 active 5.8 GHz VTX frequencies and stream timestamped RSSI samples to the host device. The SlapRF app filters the live signal stream, detects gate crossings, computes lap and section split times (S1, S2, S3), announces spoken callouts, and stores all session history in slaprf.db.

data:
Download the latest native SlapRF release from GitHub Releases . Each build is self-contained and requires no external runtime or database server.
Note The online preview at https://slaprf.app runs a simulated track for exploring the interface. Because web browsers throttle background tabs and audio, install the native Android app or desktop binary below to time real flights.
data.cli-flags#CLI Flags: Flag Default Description -addr 127.0.0.1:8090 HTTP listen address and port. -lan false Bind to 0.0.0.0:8090 for Wi-Fi LAN access (implies -no-browser). -db slaprf.db Path to the database file storing pilots, sessions, and races. -no-browser false Do not launch a browser window automatically on startup. -no-auth false Clear HTTP Basic Authentication credentials on startup. -version false Print the build version and exit.
data.platform-setup#Platform Setup:
AndroidWindowsmacOSLinux / Pi Android Open GitHub Releases on your phone or tablet and download slaprf-android-arm64.apk. Tap the downloaded .apk file to install it, allowing installation from your browser or file manager if prompted. Open SlapRF. The app runs the Go timing engine locally on your device with offline storage, spoken callouts, Bluetooth LE, and USB OTG serial support. Tip You can flash XIAO ESP32-C5 boards directly from your Android phone or tablet using the built-in Flasher screen in the SlapRF app over a USB-C data cable.
Windows Download slaprf-windows-amd64.exe from GitHub Releases . Move the executable into a dedicated folder, clear the download flag, and launch it in PowerShell (or move and double-click it in File Explorer): New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$HOME\SlapRF" | Out-Null Move-Item -Force "$HOME\Downloads\slaprf-windows-amd64.exe" "$HOME\SlapRF\slaprf.exe" Unblock-File "$HOME\SlapRF\slaprf.exe" Set-Location "$HOME\SlapRF" .\slaprf.exe SlapRF creates slaprf.db in that folder, starts on http://127.0.0.1:8090, and opens your default browser automatically. macOS Download slaprf-macos-arm64 (Apple Silicon) or slaprf-macos-amd64 (Intel) from GitHub Releases . Move the binary into a dedicated folder, clear the macOS quarantine attribute, and run it: mkdir -p ~/SlapRF && mv ~/Downloads/slaprf-macos-* ~/SlapRF/slaprf cd ~/SlapRF xattr -d com.apple.quarantine ./slaprf 2>/dev/null || true chmod +x ./slaprf ./slaprf SlapRF starts on http://127.0.0.1:8090 and opens your browser. Use Chrome, Edge, or Opera if you plan to flash firmware or connect over Web Bluetooth. Linux & Raspberry Pi Download slaprf-linux-amd64 (x86_64 PC) or slaprf-linux-arm64 (Raspberry Pi 4 / 5, 64-bit OS) from GitHub Releases . Mark the binary executable and launch it: chmod +x ./slaprf-linux-* ./slaprf-linux-amd64 For USB Hub serial access on Linux, ensure your user belongs to the serial group (dialout on Debian / Ubuntu / Raspberry Pi OS, or uucp on Arch), then log out and back in once: sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER
data.wi-fi-lan-sharing#Wi-Fi LAN Sharing:
By default, the desktop binary binds to 127.0.0.1:8090 for local use on that machine. To host SlapRF on a trackside laptop or headless Raspberry Pi so pilots and spectators can view live standings over Wi-Fi, pass -lan:
WindowsmacOS / Linux .\slaprf.exe -lan ./slaprf -lan SlapRF listens on 0.0.0.0:8090 and prints its local network URL (such as http://192.168.1.42:8090). Open Settings -> Security in the UI to set an HTTP Basic Auth username and password so spectators cannot modify race settings. If you get locked out, start the binary once with -no-auth to clear saved credentials.

data:
Build and flash DIY 5.8 GHz gate timers using off-the-shelf Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 boards with zero soldering.
Parts & Assembly Bill of materials, battery power, U.FL antenna setup, and gate placement. Flashing Firmware Flash Bluetooth Hub, USB Hub, and Spoke firmware from the SlapRF app or browser. Status LED Patterns Live animations and millisecond timing strips for every yellow LED blink state.

Configure and flash Hub (H1) and Spoke (T1 through T6) firmware onto Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 boards directly from your desktop browser below, or from the built-in Flasher screen inside the SlapRF Android and desktop apps over USB-C. No ESP-IDF toolchain, Python install, or serial driver is needed.
data.before-flashing#Before Flashing: Requirement Details Supported Host Built-in Flasher in the SlapRF Android or desktop app (over USB-C / OTG), or desktop Chrome, Edge, or Opera for the browser flasher above. USB-C Data Cable Plug directly into your phone or computer port (avoid charge-only cables and unpowered hubs). Matching Versions When updating SlapRF firmware, re-flash both the Hub (H1) and all Spokes (T1-T6) so their ESP-NOW protocol matches.
data.browser-flasher#Browser Flasher:
Connect your XIAO ESP32-C5 with a USB-C data cable in Chrome, Edge, or Opera to flash directly from this page, or flash from the Flasher screen inside the SlapRF Android or desktop app:
Open Firmware Flasher Warning Connect only one XIAO ESP32-C5 board at a time while flashing. During 2.4 GHz radio calibration bursts, each ESP32-C5 draws up to 320 mA, and plugging multiple boards into shared USB ports can cause 5 V sag and interrupted writes.
data.choose-role#Choose Role: In Step 1, pick Hub (H1, one per course) or Spoke (wireless split gates). In Step 2, choose Bluetooth (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin) or USB cable (slaprf-xiao-c5.bin) for a Hub, or pick timer slot T1 through T6 for a Spoke.
data.flash-via-usb#Flash via USB: In Step 3, click Flash H1 to USB (or T1-T6), select the USB JTAG / serial debug unit port in the browser chooser, and click Connect. Erasing, writing, and verification finish in about 20 seconds without holding the BOOT button.
data.led-quick-reference#LED Quick Reference:
After flashing, the onboard yellow LED (GPIO27) indicates board status. See Status LED Patterns for live animations and millisecond timing charts.
Board State Blink Pattern Meaning Hub Ready Single 70 ms blip every 2.0 s USB Hub active, or Bluetooth Hub connected to your paired host. Spoke Synced Double 70 ms blip every 2.0 s Spoke (T1-T6) paired with the Hub over ESP-NOW and sweeping. BLE Pairing Mode Fast double-blink every 1.0 s Unclaimed Bluetooth Hub ready to pair with a phone or laptop. Searching / Waiting Steady 1 Hz (500 ms ON / 500 ms OFF) Spoke searching for Hub, or paired BLE Hub waiting to reconnect. Identify 3 quick flashes + pause (600 ms cycle) Identify mode triggered from the SlapRF UI. Radio Fault Continuous 10 Hz strobe (50 ms ON / 50 ms OFF) 5.8 GHz radio check failed; power-cycle or re-flash the board.
data.open-flasher#Open Flasher: Click Open Firmware Flasher above to launch the 3-step firmware wizard.

data: Each battery-powered SlapRF Gate Timer snaps together from off-the-shelf parts with no soldering or custom PCBs required, and fits inside a compact 3D-printed case for field durability.
data.attach-antenna#Attach Antenna:
Align the included dual-band (2.4 / 5 GHz) U.FL antenna plug flat over the gold receptacle on the XIAO ESP32-C5 and press straight down until it clicks into place.
Warning Always snap on the U.FL antenna before applying power. Operating without the antenna severely reduces both 5.8 GHz VTX sensitivity and 2.4 GHz wireless range.
data.bill-of-materials#Bill of Materials:
One Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 draws under 100 mA at 5 V (0.5 W), so a compact 650 mAh 3S LiPo pack runs a gate timer for roughly 8 hours.
Part Purpose Example Source Est. Cost XIAO ESP32-C5 Measures 5.8 GHz VTX RSSI and communicates over ESP-NOW, Bluetooth LE, or USB-C (includes snap-on U.FL antenna). Seeed Studio $6.90 5 V USB-C BEC Steps down 3S-6S LiPo voltage to regulated 5 V USB-C power. SpeedyBee BEC AOKoda XT60 USB $8.00 - $20.00 Short USB-C Cable Short USB-C PD cable connecting the 5 V BEC output to the XIAO ESP32-C5. Short USB-C PD Cable $5.00 - $9.00 3S-6S LiPo Pack Powers the gate timer in the field (any spare XT60 flight pack or low-current USB power bank works). Tattu 850mAh 3S $15.00
data.board-layout#Board Layout: Use this callout diagram to locate the USB-C port, yellow status LED (L), U.FL antenna connector, BOOT button (B), and RESET button (R) on the XIAO ESP32-C5:
data.connect-power#Connect Power: Plug a 3S-6S LiPo battery into the XT60-to-USB-C adapter, then connect the short USB-C cable to the XIAO ESP32-C5. Set the timer flat on the ground centered inside the gate opening.
data.example-track-costs#Example Track Costs: Setup Boards Needed Typical Total 1-Gate Bluetooth 1 Bluetooth Hub (H1) + spare LiPo $23 - $35 3-Gate Bluetooth 1 Bluetooth Hub + 2 Spokes (T1, T2) $69 - $105 3-Gate Wired USB 1 USB Hub (laptop-powered) + 3 Spokes (T1-T3) $76 - $112
data.flash-firmware#Flash Firmware: Connect one XIAO ESP32-C5 at a time over USB-C to your phone (in the SlapRF Android app) or computer and flash its role using the in-app Flasher or the Flashing Firmware page. Mark each board (H1, T1, T2, T3) with tape or a paint pen so placement at the field takes seconds.
data.hardware-assembly#Hardware Assembly:
The setup below shows the barebones way to put a gate timer together using a USB-C adapter and a spare LiPo pack. While barebones wiring works right away for testing, we recommend buying or 3D printing an enclosure (see Recommended Cases below) to protect the XIAO board and U.FL antenna from prop strikes, dust, and wet grass on the course.

data.recommended-cases#Recommended Cases:
Enclosing each timer keeps the snap-on U.FL antenna strain-relieved and shields the electronics at the base of the gate. If you do not own a 3D printer, local print shops or online print services can print these STL/3MF files in PETG, ASA, or TPU for a few dollars:
Enclosure Design Highlights Model Link Compact XIAO Case Minimal snap-fit case with a USB-C cutout and dedicated internal space for the included Seeed U.FL antenna. Pair with your external USB-C adapter and LiPo pack. MakerWorld #3567817 Biscuit 18650 Tube All-in-one rugged tube enclosure that houses the XIAO ESP32-C5, internal antenna, and an integrated 18650 battery compartment in a single unit. MakerWorld #2612343 More XIAO C5 Cases Community enclosures, mounts, and gate clips designed for the Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 form factor. Browse MakerWorld
data.track-placement#Track Placement:
Center each gate timer on the ground at the base of its gate with the flat antenna element facing upward toward the flight path. Keep pilot pits and powered VTX benches at least 5 to 10 meters away from active gates so parked quads do not hold channel RSSI elevated.
On tight technical courses where an adjacent lane passes right beside a gate, placing the XIAO inside a shallow open-top metal cup or foil-lined tray shields side-lobe RF energy so only direct overhead passes register a peak.

data:
Every Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-C5 board drives its onboard yellow user LED (GPIO27) from an independent 10 ms hardware timer in the SlapRF firmware, keeping blink timing exact regardless of channel sweep load.
Each card below pairs a real-time yellow LED simulation on the left with a millisecond square-wave timing strip underneath.
data.diagnostics--faults#Diagnostics \u0026 F: LIVE Identify Timer (Find My Gate) All Boards 3 quick 50 ms flashes followed by a 350 ms pause Triggered when you click Identify on a timer in the SlapRF UI to locate which physical board corresponds to H1, T1, or T2. The 350 ms pause between 3-flash groups distinguishes it from the continuous 10 Hz fault strobe. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 3 x (50 ms ON · 50 ms OFF) + 300 ms extra dark pause (600 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Live Spectrum / Debug Stream Active (5 Hz) All Boards Steady 5 Hz fast blink Indicates an active diagnostic LIVE or wideband 5.8 GHz spectrum SCAN LIVE stream over the serial or BLE console. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 100 ms ON · 100 ms OFF (200 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE 5.8 GHz Radio Self-Check Fault (10 Hz) All Boards Continuous 10 Hz rapid strobe (no pause) The ESP32-C5 5.8 GHz radio path failed its boot or runtime health check (!rf_ok). Unplug power for 5 seconds, verify stable 5 V supply voltage, and re-flash the latest SlapRF firmware if the strobe continues. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 50 ms ON · 50 ms OFF continuous (100 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF
data.normal-operation#Normal Operation: LIVE Hub Ready & Active USB Hub · Connected Bluetooth Hub Single 70 ms blip every 2.0 seconds The Hub (H1) passed its 5.8 GHz radio self-check and is ready for timing. On a USB Hub, this pattern starts immediately after boot. On a Bluetooth Hub, it appears once your paired phone or laptop connects and authenticates over Bluetooth LE. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 70 ms ON · 1930 ms OFF (2000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Spoke Joined & Synced Spoke (T1 to T6) Double 70 ms blip every 2.0 seconds The wireless Spoke locked onto the Hub’s 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW beacon within the last 2.5 s, synchronized its clock, and is streaming 5.8 GHz RSSI sweeps to the Hub. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 70 ms ON · 150 ms OFF · 70 ms ON · 1710 ms OFF (2000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF
data.pairing--search#Pairing \u0026 Search: LIVE Bluetooth Hub: Pairing Mode (Unclaimed) Bluetooth Hub Fast double-blink every 1.0 second The Bluetooth Hub has no saved host bond yet and is open for Claim-on-Pair. Open Network in the SlapRF app and connect; the first device to connect claims the Hub so nearby spectators cannot take over your timer at the field. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 80 ms ON · 100 ms OFF · 80 ms ON · 740 ms OFF (1000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Waiting for Link (1 Hz Slow Blink) Spoke Searching · Paired Bluetooth Hub Disconnected Steady 1 Hz blink (50% duty cycle) On a Spoke (T1-T6), the board is searching for a Hub over 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW. On a claimed Bluetooth Hub (H1), the board is advertising over Bluetooth LE and waiting for its paired phone or laptop to reconnect. TIMING STRIP (2.0 s WINDOW) 500 ms ON · 500 ms OFF (1000 ms cycle) 0 ms 500 ms 1000 ms 1500 ms 2000 ms ON OFF LIVE Clear Bluetooth Pairing (Hold BOOT for 3.0 s) Bluetooth Hub Solid ON while holding BOOT -> 800 ms rapid burst -> Pairing Mode To pair a claimed Bluetooth Hub with a different phone or laptop, hold the BOOT button (GPIO28) while powered. The yellow LED stays solid ON while held, flashes a rapid 800 ms burst at 3.0 s when the saved host key is cleared, and enters Pairing Mode. TIMING STRIP (4.8 s WINDOW) Hold BOOT 3.0 s (Solid ON) -> 60 ms ON / 60 ms OFF burst (800 ms) -> Pairing Mode 0 ms 1200 ms 2400 ms 3600 ms 4800 ms ON OFF

data:
Step-by-step guides for the four most common ways pilots and race directors use SlapRF.
Solo & Club Practice Set up pilots, connect your timer, calibrate thresholds, and fly with spoken callouts. Multi-Gate Section Splits Add wireless Spoke timers around the course to measure S1, S2, and S3 split times. Running a Race Event Build brackets, run heats with automated horns, review waveforms, and sync MultiGP. RotorHazard & LapRF 8-Way Run the SlapRF Timing Application with existing RotorHazard or LapRF hardware.

Pilots and clubs who already own a RotorHazard timer or an ImmersionRC LapRF 8-Way puck can run the SlapRF Timing Application as a modern practice and race control interface without building new hardware.
Note RotorHazard and LapRF 8-Way operate as single Start / Finish multi-pilot receivers for up to 8 simultaneous channels. Multi-gate section split timing (S1, S2, S3) requires DIY SlapRF Gate Hardware.
data.connect-server#Connect Server: Open Network and click Scan LAN to discover RotorHazard servers on port 5000, or enter the server address manually (such as 192.168.1.50:5000) and click Connect.
data.connect-via-lan#Connect via LAN: Connect your LapRF 8-Way to the same router or switch as your host device. Open Network, click Scan LAN to find pucks on TCP port 5403 (or enter 192.168.1.20:5403 manually), and click Connect.
data.laprf-8-way-setup#LapRF 8-Way Setup: SlapRF communicates natively with the ImmersionRC LapRF 8-Way puck over Ethernet or Wi-Fi LAN using the binary LapRF TCP protocol (port 5403).
data.livetime-output#LiveTime Output: When running on Windows, macOS, or Linux, SlapRF can also expose a local LapRF :5403 TCP emulator so external broadcast overlays or LiveTime clients can ingest live gate crossings from SlapRF in real time.
data.rotorhazard-setup#RotorHazard Setup: SlapRF connects to an existing RotorHazard server over Wi-Fi or Ethernet (HTTP / Socket.IO) or directly to RotorHazard serial nodes over USB.
data.select-laprf#Select LapRF: Open Settings -> Hardware in the native SlapRF app and choose ImmersionRC LapRF 8-Way.
data.select-rotorhazard#Select RotorHazard: Launch the native SlapRF desktop binary or Android app, open Settings -> Hardware, and select RotorHazard.
data.sync--fly#Sync \u0026 Fly: Assign pilot VTX channels in Pilots (or inside a Race heat), click Sync on the RotorHazard card if needed, and run Practice or Race Control as usual.
data.sync-slots#Sync Slots: Confirm all 8 receiver slots report online status and pack voltage. SlapRF pushes active pilot frequencies and gain/threshold settings automatically whenever a Practice session or Race heat starts.

data: A single gate measures total lap time, while adding wireless Spoke timers (T1 through T6) around the course breaks every lap into section splits (S1, S2, S3) so you can see exactly where time is gained or lost.
data.calibrate-all#Calibrate All: Start a Practice session and fly 2 to 3 complete laps through every gate. Open Signals, keep All timers selected, and tap Calibrate all so SlapRF computes tailored Enter and Exit thresholds for each gate at once.
data.flash-spokes#Flash Spokes: Use the Firmware Flasher on a desktop computer to assign each Spoke board a unique slot (T1 through T6) on the same firmware version as H1.
data.how-splits-work#How Splits Work:
When timers sit at sequential gates along the flight path, SlapRF measures each interval independently before closing the full lap at Start / Finish:
Track Segment Recorded Split Start / Finish -> Gate 2 Section 1 (S1) Gate 2 -> Gate 3 Section 2 (S2) Last Gate -> Start / Finish Final section + completed lap time Every Spoke streams its 5.8 GHz RSSI sweeps to H1 over 2.4 GHz ESP-NOW while H1 continuously aligns each Spoke’s clock.
data.place-timers#Place Timers: In Bluetooth Hub mode, place H1 at Start / Finish and place Spokes (T1, T2, …) at split gates around the track. In USB Hub mode, keep H1 plugged into your laptop or phone at the bench, place T1 at Start / Finish, and place T2, T3, … at split gates. Raising a bench Hub onto a table or crate off damp grass improves long-range 2.4 GHz reception.
data.reading-split-data#Reading Split Data:
After flying a pack, open the Laps and Trends tabs in Practice to review performance across the track:
View What It Shows Lap Table Side-by-side S1, S2, S3 splits for every lap alongside your Theoretical Best Lap (sum of your fastest individual splits). Section Consistency Per-section variance charts highlighting which obstacle or turn costs the most time across a pack. Per-Gate Fine-Tune Select an individual timer chip (such as T2) in Signals to adjust one tight or high-speed gate without changing the rest of the course.
data.set-gate-order#Set Gate Order: Open Network to confirm H1 and all powered Spokes report Online. Open Track, drag your active timers onto the loop in exact flight order, and click the checkered flag on your Start / Finish gate.

data: Set up a single-gate practice session, calibrate RSSI thresholds for your VTX in one tap, and fly with spoken lap callouts.
data.add-pilots#Add Pilots: Open Pilots and enter each pilot’s callsign, optional phonetic spelling for text-to-speech pronunciation, and default 5.8 GHz channel (such as R1 5658 or F4 5800).
data.audio-callouts#Audio Callouts: Open Settings -> Announcer to configure practice audio. Enable Beep on Cross for an instant low-latency tone the moment a gate crossing registers, and choose whether spoken callouts read pilot name plus lap time or lap time alone.
data.connect-hub#Connect Hub: Open Network. In Bluetooth mode, power H1 at the Start / Finish gate, tap Scan / Connect, and select your SlapRF Hub. In USB mode, connect H1 over USB-C (and power T1 at Start / Finish, or place H1 at the gate) and click Connect. Confirm the timer status badge shows Online.
data.fly--calibrate#Fly \u0026 Calibrate: Open Practice, select the active pilots, tap Start, and switch to the Signals tab. Arm your quad, fly 2 to 3 clean passes through the Start / Finish gate at normal race speed, then tap Calibrate. SlapRF inspects your signal peaks and noise floor and sets the Enter and Exit dBm levels automatically.
data.hardware-mode#Hardware Mode: Open Settings -> Hardware and choose SlapRF (Bluetooth) if your Hub runs slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin on battery power at the gate, or SlapRF (USB) if your Hub plugs into your device over USB-C.
data.prerequisites#Prerequisites: Install the SlapRF Timing Application on your Android phone or laptop and prepare one flashed Hub timer (H1, either Bluetooth or USB).
data.threshold-tuning#Threshold Tuning:
Most setups need no manual adjustment after tapping Calibrate. To fine-tune a specific gate, select its timer chip in Signals and open Fine-tune:
Parameter Adjustment Guide Enter Threshold (dBm) Signal level that starts a crossing. Raise it (closer to 0 dBm) if nearby lanes trigger false laps; lower it if fast passes are missed. Exit Threshold (dBm) Signal level that closes the crossing window (6 to 12 dBm below Enter prevents double-triggers). Min Lap Time (s) Minimum seconds between consecutive valid laps for the same pilot. Any timer chip or global rule with custom overrides shows a small blue pencil indicator. Tap Clear calibration at any time to restore default values.
data.verify-track#Verify Track: Open Track and confirm your active gate timer (H1 or T1) sits on the course loop with the checkered Start / Finish flag selected.

data: SlapRF includes a full race control workspace for club races, qualifiers, elimination brackets, and MultiGP chapter events.
data.create-or-import#Create or Import:
Open Races from the main navigation to start a new event:
Option Workflow Built-in Templates Start from Qualifying + Finals, Double Elimination, Single Elimination, Open Qualifier, Points Mains, Chase the Ace, or a Blank Custom Format. MultiGP Import Add your chapter API key in Settings -> MultiGP to pull registered pilots, VTX channels, and event rounds directly from MultiGP.
data.format--heats#Format \u0026 Heats:
Inside an event workspace, open Setup to configure stages, advancement rules, and heat lineups using either editor:
Format Canvas: Drag stage nodes and connect advancement wires visually (for example, routing Top 8 from Qualifying to Championship Double Elimination and 9th-16th to Consolation). Setup Table: Edit heat counts, pilot slots, VTX channels, heat duration, and scoring format (Fastest 3 Consecutive, Single Fastest Lap, Total Laps + Time, Points, or Chase the Ace). Tip Enable Simulator mode before race day to test custom stage progressions, advancement rules, and heat tie-breakers end to end without hardware.
data.live-race-control#Live Race Control:
Switch to the Race tab when pilots step up to the flight line:
Select the upcoming heat and confirm pilot VTX channel assignments. Click Start Heat. SlapRF plays the staging callout, runs the configured start delay, sounds the start horn, and arms crossing detection. During the heat, live standings, split deltas, and spoken lead/lap announcements update in real time. When the clock expires, the finish horn sounds while timing stays open until active pilots finish their current lap. Click Next Heat to advance; when a stage completes, downstream brackets seed automatically.
data.marshal-review#Marshal Review: When a pilot challenges a missed crossing or an early launch, open the completed heat’s review panel in Race Control to inspect the recorded Start / Finish RSSI waveform alongside every crossing marker. Race directors can invalidate a false pass, insert a missed crossing at its exact waveform peak, or schedule a re-run, with standings updating immediately.
data.results--multigp#Results \u0026 MultiGP: Open the podium view at any time to inspect overall event standings. For MultiGP chapter races, click Upload to MultiGP to publish completed round times and final placements back to your MultiGP event page.

data:
Screen-by-screen UI documentation, timing detection parameters, and troubleshooting solutions.
App & UI Reference Guide to every SlapRF screen and the 3-tier timing rules. Troubleshooting Solutions for flashing, Bluetooth, Spoke pairing, and gate detection.
Quick diagnostics and fixes for USB flashing, wireless connectivity, power supplies, and gate detection.
data.false-adjacent-laps#False Adjacent Laps:
If flying on a nearby lane triggers laps on an adjacent gate:
Fly 2 to 3 clean passes through the gate and click Calibrate, or open Fine-tune and raise the Enter threshold closer to 0 dBm (for example, -58 dBm to -50 dBm). Set Min Lap Time just below your fastest realistic lap on the course. On tight tracks, set the XIAO inside a shallow open-top metal cup or foil-lined tray under the gate to block side-lobe RF from neighboring lanes.
data.hub-not-found#Hub Not Found:
If your phone or laptop does not discover the Bluetooth Hub in Network:
Verify the board was flashed with the Bluetooth Hub image (slaprf-xiao-c5-ble.bin) and shows either the fast double-blink (Pairing Mode) or 1 Hz slow blink. Confirm Settings -> Hardware is set to SlapRF (Bluetooth). Disconnect any other phone or browser tab already linked to the Hub (BLE advertising pauses while an active host is connected). To pair with a new host, hold BOOT on the Hub for 3.0 s until the rapid LED burst clears the previous bond.
data.interrupted-flash#Interrupted Flash: If flashing halts partway through or boards reset randomly on USB, unplug any extra XIAO boards so only one board is connected at a time. Multiple ESP32-C5 radios calibrating on 2.4 GHz simultaneously can droop a shared laptop 5 V rail.
data.missed-fast-passes#Missed Fast Passes:
If high-speed passes through a gate do not register:
Confirm the pilot’s channel in Pilots matches the exact VTX band and frequency (and that Pit Mode is off). Remove inactive pilot slots from the session so timers sweep fewer frequencies and sample each active pilot faster. Open Fine-tune on that gate timer and lower the Enter threshold slightly (for example, -48 dBm to -55 dBm).
data.power-bank-shutoff#Power Bank Shutoff: Because a XIAO ESP32-C5 draws under 100 mA, some phone power banks assume nothing is connected and shut off after 30 to 60 seconds. Power gate timers from a 3S-6S LiPo pack with an XT60-to-USB-C 5 V BEC (which never auto-sleeps), or enable trickle-charge mode on your power bank.
data.spoke-stays-offline#Spoke Stays Offline:
If a Spoke (T1-T6) blinks slowly at 1 Hz and stays offline in Network:
Power on the Hub (H1) first and verify it is online. Re-flash the Hub and all Spokes from the same SlapRF release so their ESP-NOW packet versions match. Check that the snap-on U.FL antenna is firmly seated on both boards and that no two Spokes share the same slot ID (T1-T6):
data.usb-port-missing#USB Port Missing:
If the XIAO ESP32-C5 does not appear in the browser serial port chooser:
Swap to a known USB-C data cable (many bundled cables are charge-only with no data wires). Plug directly into your Android phone (using the SlapRF app) or a computer USB port rather than an unpowered hub or dock (use desktop Chrome, Edge, or Opera if flashing from a web browser). On Linux, confirm your user is in the dialout or uucp group so /dev/ttyACM0 can be opened. If a board is unresponsive, hold the tiny BOOT button (B, bottom-right of the XIAO) while plugging in USB-C, release BOOT, and click Flash to USB:

data: Reference guide to the screens, live signal scope controls, and crossing detection parameters in the SlapRF Timing Application.
data.app-screens#App Screens: Screen Purpose Practice Open or timed practice sessions with live lap tables, Signals (5.8 GHz RSSI scope and calibration), and Trends (progression and split consistency charts). Races Event creation, MultiGP import, visual Format Canvas brackets, live Race Control horns, and Marshal Review waveforms. Pilots Pilot directory with callsigns, phonetic TTS spellings, and default 5.8 GHz channels (Raceband, Fatshark, Boscam, IMD6). Track Visual course loop editor for ordering active gate timers (H1, T1-T6) and marking the Start / Finish gate. Network Connection manager and live packet-rate monitor for SlapRF Bluetooth Hub, SlapRF USB Hub, RotorHazard, and LapRF 8-Way. Flasher Built-in wizard (on Android and desktop) for flashing Hub and Spoke firmware, inspecting board configuration, or factory-erasing boards over USB-C. Simulator Multi-pilot 5.8 GHz physics track simulator for testing track layouts, threshold behavior, and race brackets without hardware. Settings Hardware backend selector, Announcer voice & horn levels, MultiGP API key, HTTP Basic Auth, theme toggle, and .json database backup/restore.
data.crossing-rules#Crossing Rules:
SlapRF runs a hysteresis detector (Enter dBm -> peak tracking -> Exit dBm) governed by global rules that can also be overridden per gate in Fine-tune:
Parameter Role Enter Threshold (dBm) RSSI level required to open a crossing window. Exit Threshold (dBm) RSSI level required to close the crossing window and record the peak timestamp (6 to 12 dBm below Enter prevents double-counting). Min Crossing Time (s) Minimum duration RSSI must remain inside the crossing window, rejecting brief single-sample RF noise spikes (SPIKE). Min Lap Time (s) Minimum valid lap time between consecutive Start / Finish crossings for the same pilot (MIN_LAP). Max Lap Time (s) Maximum duration before a long pause (such as landing to swap batteries) starts a fresh out-lap instead of recording a slow lap (LAP_TOO_LONG). Beep on Cross Plays an immediate low-latency audio tone when a crossing registers, ahead of the spoken lap callout.
data.signals-controls#Signals Controls:
Available inside Practice -> Signals and Race -> Signals:
Control Behavior Prev | Live | Next Pause and scrub backward or forward through recorded RSSI history, or return to live streaming. Auto X Switch the horizontal scope span between 1 s, 15 s, 60 s, 5 min, 10 min, or automatic fit. Auto Y Toggle automatic vertical dBm range fitting versus full dBm scale. Timer Chips Filter by All, H1, or T1-T6 to view or edit Enter and Exit lines. A blue pencil icon marks chips with custom overrides. Calibrate Compute optimal Enter and Exit dBm levels from recent flight passes, or tap Clear calibration to restore defaults.
